  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from Slurm)

# Slurm requested:
#   -p long
#   --job-name=HEPG2_rna_seq
#   --mail-type=END,FAIL
#   --mail-user=john.rinn@colorado.edu
#   --nodes=1
#   --ntasks=1
#   --mem=6gb
#   --time=20:00:00
#   --output=nextflow.out
#   --error=nextflow.err

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  -n 1 \
  --time=20h \
  --queue=long \
  bash -lc '

# Approximate Slurm --output/--error by shell redirection.
exec >nextflow.out 2>nextflow.err

# NOTE: Slurm --mem=6gb has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.

# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

pwd; hostname; date

echo "Here we go You\x27ve requested ${FLUX_RESOURCE_NCORES:-unknown} core."
# (Slurm referenced $SLURM_CPUS_ON_NODE; Flux does not provide a universally portable equivalent.)

module load singularity/3.1.1

nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq -r 1.4.2 \
  -resume \
  -profile singularity \
  --reads "/scratch/Shares/rinnclass/CLASS_2022/JR/CLASS_2022/class_exeRcises/analysis/17_API_RNASEQ/fastq/*{_read1,_read2}.fastq.gz" \

  --gtf /scratch/Shares/rinnclass/CLASS_2022/data/gencode.v32.annotation.gtf \
  --pseudo_aligner salmon \
  --gencode \
  --email john.rinn@colorado.edu \
  -c nextflow.config

date
'
"
